title: feat(app-shell): the object and app-nav icon fields pick from the icon catalog, and the picker warns on an unknown name (objectui#12531)
body:
Fixes #12531
Clause-②: no. Inspector fields and the icon picker's own warning, all inside `@object-ui/app-shell`: no type, prop, export or spec change.

## What changed

- **`ObjectDefaultInspector`** (the object designer's Basics panel, which Studio's Object Settings mounts): the Icon field is now `IconPickerWidget`, the picker the action inspector and the Studio nav inspector already mount. Its `Label` names it (`htmlFor` + `useId`). Clearing patches `icon: undefined`, the convention the text field had. The field's hint `designer.object.iconHint` ("Lucide icon name (e.g. building, users)") is retired from both locale blocks (en, zh) in the same commit, with the text field it described.
- **`AppNavInspector`**: an entry for which `navEntryOffersField(entryType, 'icon')` holds gets the same picker. A separator still gets no icon field. Clearing writes `icon: ''`, the convention the text field had (the spec takes it).
- Both hosts pass their read-only posture through as the picker's `readOnly`, as the text fields took `disabled={readOnly}`.
- **`IconPickerWidget`**: a stored name that matches no icon in the catalog it offers shows an inline warning under the trigger, from one new key, `engine.form.unknownIcon` (en and zh): No icon is named “NAME”. Choose one from the list. The trigger is `aria-describedby` the warning. It replaces the "(not in object)" flag the trigger used to show beside such a name. That flag was the field picker's copy (`engine.form.notInObject`, still used by the field pickers). The warning is inside the widget, so every mount gets it: the two fields above, the action inspector, the Studio nav inspector, and `SchemaForm`'s `icon` widget.
- No second picker component, nothing moved to `packages/components`. The icon set and the stored value's shape (a Lucide name string) are unchanged.

## Mechanism readings (the dispatch's assumptions, measured)

- **A1, partly confirmed.** `IconPickerWidget` searches `iconNames` from `lucide-react/dynamic.mjs`. That is the same set `LazyIcon` / `getLazyIcon` resolve against, so "matches no icon" in the picker is exactly "falls back" in the resolvers. It previews the current icon on its trigger. Two parts of card target 1 it does not do: (a) it is a modal dialog, not a popover; (b) a name can be typed only as a search query and then picked, so a name outside the catalog cannot be committed by typing. Neither was changed here, per the ruling that limits `widgets.tsx` to the warning. Before this PR it flagged an unknown name only with the field picker's "(not in object)". I read that as no warning on an unknown icon name, so the warning was added inside the widget.
- **A2, confirmed with a split.** `ObjectDefaultInspector` committed `onPatch({ icon: v || undefined })`, so empty means `undefined`, and that is kept. `AppNavInspector` committed `patch({ icon: v })`, so empty means `''`. That is kept too: the picker's clear sends `undefined`, and the host maps it to `''`.
- **A3, retired.** `designer.object.iconHint` described typing a Lucide name. The picker previews and searches instead, so the key is removed from the en and zh blocks. No other reader exists (`git grep` over the tree finds none).
- **The rail tile's fallback, already in place.** The Data pillar's rail row and item header draw `getIcon(o.icon)` / `getIcon(...)`, and `getIcon` is `getLazyIcon`, which returns the `Database` glyph for an unknown name. That is the same glyph it returns for no name. So the card's "a misspelt name renders nothing" does not hold on today's `main`: it draws the generic glyph. This is pinned in `IconPickerWidget.unknownName-12531.test.tsx`: `getIcon('not-an-icon')` is `getIcon(undefined)` is `Database`, and a catalog name is not `Database`. `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` is not edited.

## Tests

New:
- `IconPickerWidget.unknownName-12531.test.tsx`: the key is a real en and zh row carrying the name placeholder. `not-an-icon` shows the warning, naming the value, and the trigger is described by it. CONTROL: `building`, `Building2` and an empty value show none. Picking `building` over the unknown name clears the warning. The zh copy renders under a zh `I18nProvider`. CONTROL: the action inspector's icon field still shows `check` and writes a picked `building`, and now warns on an unknown name. The rail fallback pin.
- `ObjectDefaultInspector.iconPicker-12531.test.tsx`: the Icon field is a combobox named "Icon" and no text box. Typing `build` lists `building`, and picking it patches `{ icon: 'building' }`. An unknown stored name warns, and a catalog name does not. Clearing patches `icon: undefined`. Read-only disables it.
- `AppNavInspector.iconPicker-12531.test.tsx`: an object entry renders the picker, named "Icon". Picking `building` writes `icon: 'building'`, and the entry parses as `NavigationItemSchema`. Clearing writes `icon: ''`, which also parses. An unknown name warns. Read-only disables it. CONTROL: a separator renders no icon field.

Updated, because they typed into the old text input: `ObjectDefaultInspector.test.tsx` (the commit leg and the read-only leg) and `AppNavInspector.separatorFields-11847.test.tsx` (the CONTROL leg now picks `chart-bar` through the picker).

Runs at head `62e216dfb5` (after merging `main`):
- every suite naming `IconPickerWidget`, `ObjectDefaultInspector`, `AppNavInspector` or `ActionDefaultInspector`, plus both icon-widget files: `Test Files 28 passed (28)`, `Tests 335 passed (335)`;
- the widget-registry and designer-i18n-table readers, plus the census and ratchet suites whose subject this touches: `Test Files 33 passed (33)`, `Tests 686 passed (686)`;
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0, after building the dependency closure (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all five touched test files.

**Ablation (one host back to a text input).** The implementation was committed first. `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack) replaced the `IconPickerWidget` element in `ObjectDefaultInspector.tsx` with the old `InspectorTextField`: anchor x1 to x0, blob `84b4270f6c10` to `a99d7b0cc0da`. Then `ObjectDefaultInspector.iconPicker-12531.test.tsx` ran: `Tests 5 failed (5)`. The tool restored the file: blob back to the HEAD blob `84b4270f6c10`, and `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Gates (local subset, at `62e216dfb5`)

Each command's exit code was captured before any pipe; all exit 0:
- `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:i18n-designer-parity`;
- `check:i18n-dead-keys` (report-only; it lists neither key touched here);
- `check:icon-record-names`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:metadata-write-doors`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources`;
- `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations);
- `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
- `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`.

ESLint on the nine changed TS/TSX files: 0 errors. Every warning sits on an unchanged line. `scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the diff: NOT GOVERNED. The full farm (`pnpm test` shards, `pnpm lint`, the rest of `ci.yml`, `lint.yml` and `performance-budget.yml`) is CI's. `Spec Main Shape Gate` has been red on `main` (objectui#12464) and is advisory here.

## What the landing seat's browser reading should show

On the vite console (dark and light):
1. Studio › Data › an object › Settings › Basics › Icon is a combobox showing the current icon's glyph and name, not a text input. The "Lucide icon name" hint line is gone.
2. Clicking it opens "Choose an icon". Typing `build` narrows the grid to the none tile, `building-2` and `building`. Clicking `building` closes the dialog, the trigger shows the building glyph, and the rail row and item header draw it.
3. An object whose stored icon matches no icon (seed one through the metadata API, since the picker cannot write one) shows the generic glyph and the name on the trigger, and, under it, an amber line with a warning triangle: No icon is named “NAME”. Choose one from the list. Its rail row and item header draw the generic `Database` glyph, the same as an object with no icon.
4. Setup › an app › a navigation entry of type object or page: the Icon field is the same picker. On a separator, no Icon field.
5. The action editor's icon picker looks as before, except that an unknown stored name now shows the same warning and no longer shows "(not in object)".

A throwaway Vite harness (not committed) rendered both inspectors with the console's Tailwind build, light and dark. It confirmed the warning text on both hosts, the `build` search listing `building-2` and `building`, and that picking clears the warning. Those screenshots stay out of `main`, per the maintainer's ruling.

## Acceptance notes

- The action inspector's icon `Label` is not tied to its picker (no `htmlFor` / `id`), so that combobox has no accessible name "Icon". This PR's CONTROL test has to find it by `aria-haspopup="dialog"`. This is out of scope here and is reported to the seat as a finding.
- Setup's nav editor clears an entry icon to `''`, kept as found. Studio's nav inspector removes the key. Both parse, and both draw the target's fallback. This is an observation, not filed. Carrier: none.
- `check:i18n-dead-keys` reports `engine.form.keep` as confirmed-dead (the picker's keep option uses its value as its title). It is pre-existing and was not touched. Carrier: none.
- The picker's own strings follow the `I18nProvider` language (`useMetadataLocale`), not a host inspector's `locale` prop. This is pre-existing on every mount and was not touched.
